sections.h2: Which Rowan County offices assess and bill property?
sections.html:
Rowan County Tax Administration has two divisions, the Assessor's office and the Tax Collector's office. The Assessor lists, assesses and bills all taxable property in the county, and the collector takes payment. The real property appraisers can be reached at 704-216-8586, and the county directs listing questions to 704-216-8558.

The county says it is building an electronic online listing process that should be ready for the 2027 listing season. Until then, ask the office how to list personal property, such as a boat, a camper or a mobile home, each January.

Rowan County Tax Assessor pages link to a land records map tool. Sellers there will deal with the county bill and with any municipal or district bill that applies to the parcel, so check the tax record for every levy before you list.

sections.h2: When does Rowan County revalue property?
sections.html:
Every four years. The county's page gives January 1, 2023 as the last revaluation and January 1, 2027 as the next, with a further one scheduled for January 2031.

State law sets only an outer limit of eight years. Rowan's page says the shorter cycle softens sticker shock, and it adds that revaluation never sets a rate, since commissioners set rates in the yearly budget. Values come from actual sales.

Rowan County revaluation timeline as printed on the county page

A seller close to a revaluation date should expect buyers to study the new assessed value, because it drives the bill they will inherit. The county also says value follows the condition of a parcel on January 1, so tell the assessor about any building added, moved or torn down.

sections.h2: What did the 2023 revaluation do to Rowan County values?
sections.html:
Real property values rose by an average of 44.96% from the prior period, according to the county's revaluation page. The county reports that almost 12,000 residential and 700 business property sales from January 1, 2019 through December 31, 2022 went into that work.

The same page shows the county's total taxable base moving from about $14.4 billion to a projected $18.5 billion, with real property revalued to about $15.5 billion. Other categories such as vehicles, personal property and utilities fell, so the rise in total base was 28.5% against a 44.96% jump for real estate alone. County law also required a revenue-neutral rate to be reported to the commissioners, who could lower the rate to ease the increase.

For a seller, the lesson is that a revaluation can reset the bill sharply for the buyer, even when the rate drops. Check the current assessed value on the county's parcel tools before pricing, and keep in mind the next reset in 2027.

sections.h2: What is the COMPER tool for Rowan County owners?
sections.html:
COMPER is an online tool that shows the valid sales the tax office uses to help set values in the 2027 cycle. You enter a property address and receive a list and a map of valid sales between January 1, 2023 and December 31, 2026 within a five-mile radius.

From that list you can pick sales similar to your home and turn them into a printable or PDF report. The map includes a street view of each comparable property. A Rowan County seller can use the same report to check a listing price against what the assessor treats as valid sales, though the tool does not replace an agent's or appraiser's opinion.

sections.h2: What is the path for disputing a Rowan County assessment?
sections.html:
Call the tax office before anything else, then use the written form if the call does not settle it. The county says informal talks usually happen from January through March. Its revaluation page tells owners to fill in the Real Property Appeal Form and attach supporting papers, and warns that a review can leave the number alone, cut it or raise it.

The formal stage works like this:

  • Real property appeals must arrive before the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns for the year.
  • That Board meets for the first time sometime between early April and early May. The county publishes notice in a local paper three times, beginning at least 10 days ahead.
  • Each side gets time to speak. The Board may rule at once or deliberate, and the owner should receive the ruling in writing.
  • Beyond that sits the Property Tax Commission, which meets monthly in Raleigh and behaves like a trial court. The owner carries the burden of proof, and companies and LLCs need a North Carolina attorney.

Personal property follows a shorter clock of 30 days from the first notice of value, and when no separate notice goes out, the bill itself is the notice. After the Board adjourns it may still take up discovered property, classified vehicles, audits and personal property cases.

sections.h2: When are Rowan County taxes due?
sections.html:
September 1 is the due date under state law, and no interest accrues until January 6. After that, two percent applies through the end of January, then three-fourths of a percent for each additional month or part of one.

Counties may adopt a prepayment discount by resolution before May 1. Confirm any discount, card fee or payment channel with the Rowan County Tax Collector, since those details are set locally.

Personal property listing takes place in January, and the commissioners may extend it. The county says an online listing process is being built for the 2027 listing season.

sections.h2: What relief programs can Rowan County owners use?
sections.html:
The county's Exemptions page describes three state programs, and each applicant is limited to one. Applications for the elderly or disabled, disabled veteran and circuit breaker programs are due by June 1 of the year of application. Other exemptions are filed in January.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of the first $25,000 or half of appraised value, for owners aged 65 or up or fully and permanently disabled, with 2026 household income no higher than $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: up to the first $45,000. An unremarried surviving spouse can qualify, and age and income play no role.
  • Circuit breaker: an owner of five years or more with income up to $58,200 may defer tax above 4% of income at or under $38,800, or above 5% in the higher band.

On the circuit breaker, multiple owners must all qualify, and you must reapply each year. The deferred tax is a lien, and the most recent three years come due with interest if the owner transfers, dies or stops using the home as a residence. Present-use value applications are filed each January, or after a value change notice.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid taxes when I sell my Rowan County house?
sections.html:
The sale proceeds cover them, because each year's lien sticks to the parcel from the January listing date, along with interest and costs. A lien for personal property tax can reach all of the owner's real estate inside the taxing unit.

Left unpaid, a bill can lead to a suit and an auction of the parcel. Until the court confirms that sale, the owner can still redeem by clearing the tax and its extras.

Ask the Rowan County Tax Collector for a written payoff on each parcel and hand it to your closing attorney. Anyone planning a quick sale should do this first, since back taxes shape both price and timing.

faqs.q: When is Rowan County's next revaluation?
faqs.a: The county's page says the next revaluation takes effect January 1, 2027, and that the following one is scheduled for January 2031 on a four-year cycle.

faqs.q: What is the first move if my Rowan County value looks wrong?
faqs.a: Call the tax office, since informal reviews usually run January through March. If that fails, send the Real Property Appeal Form with your evidence before the county board adjourns.

faqs.q: What is the deadline on a Rowan County personal property valuation?
faqs.a: Thirty days from the first notice of value. Without a separate notice, the tax bill serves as that notice.
COMPER is the county's online comparison tool. Enter an address to see valid sales from January 1, 2023 through December 31, 2026 within five miles, and build a report from similar homes.

faqs.q: Who do I call at the Rowan County Tax Assessor?
faqs.a: Real property appraisers are at 704-216-8586, and the county lists 704-216-8558 for listing questions. The office also has an email contact on its Tax Assessor page.
